subject: Gateway SDK back-compat negotiation with Blueforge Labs
messages:
From: Emily Tan <e.tan@blueforge.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: integrations@blueforge.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway SDK roadmap — compatibility ask

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Blueforge is excited about the gateway routing stuff. We did a quick audit of our customer's installed base and a planned breaking change to the SDK transport layer would affect several active integrations.

High level ask: can Redwood commit to a compatibility window for any v2 transport/packaging changes (minimum 9 months) and provide a migration shim or guidance so our managed customers don't hit production regressions?

I've attached a short requirements doc and a compatibility matrix showing the >20 installs we'd need covered. We're also interested in an optional compatibility testing run with your infra team (we can share a test harness).

Main constraints:
- Many enterprise customers pin to SDK semver and run quarterly maintenance windows.
- Our managed services group cannot perform hot fixes without an architectural rollback plan.

Would love to schedule a 30-min sync next week with product/engineering to align the timelines.

Best,
Emily
Integration Lead
Blueforge Labs

Attachment: bf_compatibility_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 76KB)

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tan <e.tan@blueforge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway SDK roadmap — compatibility ask

Hi Emily — thanks for the doc and matrix, and for outlining the install footprint. Appreciate the clarity.

Short answers first:
- Redwood is open to guaranteeing a 9-month compatibility window for v2 transport changes as long as we formalize the migration contract (feature gates, deprecation notices, and a documented shim).
- We can offer a joint compatibility test run (our infra/QA + your harness) during the canary period.

Requests from our side:
1) Can you enumerate the top 5 enterprise customers affected and whether they require air-gapped deploys?
2) For any customers on older TLS/tooling chains, do you want us to produce a backwards-compatible client bundle or a Kubernetes init container shim?
3) Please confirm whether any of the installs run on-prem without outbound telemetry — that will change our rollback approach.

I'm looping Marcus (product) and Vanessa (partnerships) to scope the internal work and to surface potential contract implications. Proposed next steps:
- 30-min cross-org call on Tue 2027-04-20 10:00 PT
- Blueforge shares a sanitized subset of the compatibility matrix ahead of the call
- Redwood to draft a migration/rollback template (we can send a first pass by end of day Mon)

If the timeslot works I'll calendar invite.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_proposed_rollback_plan.pdf (stub)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Tan <e.tan@blueforge.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Gateway SDK roadmap — compatibility ask

Thanks for looping me in. Quick product view:

- We are planning the transport refactor in the Oct quarter (internal codename: transport-v2). The change delivers ~18% latency improvement at the cost of removing the legacy framing header we currently surface.
- We can preserve a compatibility layer for 9 months but it will cost engineering cycles: estimate 2.5 engineer-months for a maintained shim + 1 engineer-month for test harness automation.
- We should include a feature-flagged rollout and a deprecation timeline in contract addenda; I've penciled a migration window of 9 months with quarterly opt-in for targeted customers.

Operational asks for the Blueforge call:
1) An anonymized list of the 5 highest-risk customers (for prioritization)
2) Confirmation on whether Blueforge will accept a phased compatibility bundle (K8s init container + compatibility client) vs a full LTS client.

I'll draft an internal estimate for PM/eng and attach to the call notes. Vanessa — can you check whether partnerships is comfortable with a SLA addendum for the compatibility window? If partners want a longer guarantee we'll need to price it as a billable add-on.

-Marcus
Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Tan <e.tan@blueforge.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway SDK roadmap — compatibility ask

Thanks — the Tue slot works for our team. We've sanitized the matrix and attached the small subset you'll need for triage.

Answers inline:
- Top-five (anonymized): Customer A (on-prem, no outbound), Customer B (air-gapped), Customer C (cloud, pinned to older SDK), Customer D (managed service with strict maintenance windows), Customer E (appliance-based).
- Blueforge prefers a phased compatibility bundle (K8s init container + compatibility client) as the default; we will escalate to a full LTS client for Customer B only if negotiations require it.
- We can run a joint compatibility test the week after the call; my engineering lead will be on the sync.

Attachments: blueforge_backcompat_requirements.docx, bf_compatibility_matrix_v1.xlsx

Looking forward to the call.

Emily
Integration Lead
Blueforge Labs
